summary: Regenerated against design-spec.md v3. openart was correctly not invoked — every value in this spec is a precise token lifted from the live Home.jsx, so an AI-generated image would blur exact values; this is unchanged reasoning from prior passes. Rebuilt preview.html with the v3-fixed additive surface scale (macOS rgba(255,244,230,0.055) vs. Windows rgba(255,244,230,0.028), both against INK) and re-rendered all three isolated widths (390/1280/1440) via headless Chrome (CDP Page.captureScreenshot at deviceScaleFactor 1, matching the prior pass's convention) — visually confirmed the macOS card now composites brighter than the Windows card on every channel, fixing the measured hierarchy inversion from critique pass 2. Also fixed the Windows action-slot register (15px/400/left-aligned) and replaced the invented 'macOS 12+' claim with the literal bracketed placeholder 'macOS ⟨MIN VERSION — TBC⟩' per spec §8's new rule — confirmed rendering as visibly unresolved text in the screenshot, not a plausible number. Built the new required in-context render: preview-context.html assembles the real Pricing section tail (LIGHT_BG/LIGHT_INK, real plans data) and the real Closing CTA head (INK, real centered bloom, real blockquote) verbatim from Home.jsx around the fixed Download section, using two zero-height marker spans measured via CDP Runtime.evaluate to locate the exact section seams, then cropped with PIL to [seam1-200px .. seam2+400px] at 1440px width. The resulting preview-context-1440.png directly answers both open questions from spec §12: the light→dark seam at the Pricing boundary is clean, not abrupt, and the Download orb reads as a quiet setup for the Closing CTA's brighter bloom rather than competing with it — the 'Download glows, Closing CTA blooms' rule holds up under an actual in-context render. No blocking issues found in this render pass; all three v3 fixes (surface hierarchy, placeholder literalism, in-context adjacency) are independently visible in the rendered artifacts, not just asserted in spec text.
